observations: Photo 0 shows the front of a Canon EOS 700D box with an EF-S 18-55 IS STM lens.
Photo 1 shows the back of the same box with a barcode, serial number, and Chinese text indicating 'Made in Japan' and 'Made in Taiwan'.
Photo 2 shows the side of the box with the Canon logo and model name.
All photos show the box only; no camera or lens is visible outside the packaging.
The box appears to be in good condition with no visible damage.

claims.evidence: The box is labeled 'Made in Japan' and 'Made in Taiwan' in photo 1, which contradicts the 'UK used' claim. No proof of origin or usage history is visible.
Photo 0 box clearly states '18.0 MEGA PIXELS CMOS'.
The ISO range is not fully visible in the photos; the text is cut off or partially obscured.

claims.claim: Shutter count under 5,000, no fungus or scratch on the lens. Original battery and charger, never repaired.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The camera may be non-functional or have internal damage not visible in the box.
risks.proof: A video showing the camera powering on, menu navigation, and taking a photo.

risks.risk: The lens may be damaged or missing components (e.g., filter, cap, or internal parts).
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the lens barrel and front element, and a video showing the lens being removed and reinserted.
risks.if_unproven: priced as lens missing or damaged

risks.risk: The camera may be a counterfeit or rebranded unit.
risks.proof: A photo of the camera's serial number and a comparison with official Canon documentation or a video of the camera's menu showing the model name.

proof_requests: Video of the camera powering on and taking a photo.
Close-up photo of the lens barrel and front element.
Photo of the camera's serial number and a comparison with official Canon documentation.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
